privacy_review.basis: Contains security contract labels and credential-type names only; no User, Session, credential, Institution, request, or operational data.

assets.alt: One cookie or bearer credential passes through transport validation, CSRF protection where required, and the route's declared assurance checks to establish an immutable principal. The principal contains identity and assurance, not permission. The owning use case combines it with an action and exact resource, reads current PostgreSQL authority, and durably records allow or deny.
assets.caption: Transport proof establishes an immutable principal, not permission. The owning use case separately evaluates current action-and-resource authority and can proceed only after its allow decision is durably recorded.

privacy_review.basis: Contains canonical domain labels and generic relationship descriptions only; no Institution, Academic Unit, Programme, Class, User, enrollment, or operational data.

assets.alt: One Institution owns a hierarchy of Academic Units. Each Academic Unit may own child units and Programmes; each Programme owns Programme Levels; and each Class is one concrete roster under a Programme Level. Academic Periods may be Institution-owned and apply everywhere, or Academic-Unit-owned and apply to that unit and its descendants. Every Class explicitly names exactly one Academic Period applicable to its Programme's Academic Unit.
assets.caption: Academic Units may recurse, but Programme, Programme Level, and Class ownership is singular. A Class explicitly names one applicable Institution- or Academic-Unit-owned Period; Proctor never infers a global current Period.

privacy_review.basis: Contains canonical examination states and generic relationship descriptions only; no Exam, Class, User, Attempt, Submission, schedule, reason, answer, or operational data.

assets.alt: An Exam owns one mutable revision-fenced Draft. Publishing freezes an immutable numbered Exam Revision before an Exam Sitting selects it with one eligible Class and an explicit time window. The first eligible connection creates one Exam Attempt for the student and Sitting; submission or Sitting closure seals one terminal Submission.
assets.caption: Publishing separates mutable authoring from immutable delivery. Sitting and Attempt transitions remain PostgreSQL-authoritative, and both voluntary submission and automatic Sitting closure converge on one terminal Submission with no reopen or resubmission.

assets.alt: The root Makefile owns the local development lifecycle. Its optional Vite process proxies browser API and WebSocket traffic to the foreground Proctor server. The server uses health-checked PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, and Mailpit services. Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and the OpenTelemetry Collector are reconstructible diagnostic services, while generated configuration, secrets, and logs remain under ignored build state.
assets.caption: The root Makefile owns one reproducible local lifecycle: the server remains foreground-visible, dependencies are health-checked, observability is reconstructible, and generated secrets and state remain ignored outputs.
